shortDefinition: An AI model whose trained parameters are publicly released, allowing anyone to run and modify it.
fullDefinition: An open-weights model (often loosely called 'open-source') is one whose model parameters (weights) are publicly released. This allows anyone to download, run, fine-tune, and redistribute the model. Examples include Meta's Llama, Mistral, Gemma, and Phi. Open-weights models enable local AI, custom deployments, and experimentation without cloud dependency — but typically trail frontier closed models in capability.
examples: Meta Llama 3 — can be downloaded and run locally via Ollama
Mistral 7B — small enough to run on a laptop
